Problem Navigator

Any problem, any domain. Name the type, run its 4 beats, close the same way every time.

Step Say it out loud Trap Example
Step 0 · first 45 seconds

Hear it, then write 3 lines

"Let me restate: [the prompt in one line]. I'll aim to [read it / diagnose it / design for it]."

Problem: ______________
Who: ______________
Moves: type + 3 beats
TrapSpeaking before writing. Asking "is that correct?" after the restatement.
ExampleProblem: casual players stop after week 1. Who: casual player with spare 5 minutes. Moves: design.
Step 1 · 10 seconds

Name the type

"This sounds like a [type] problem."

Ask yourself: what did they hand me? Pick one below.

IF TWO TYPES FIT, THE VERB IN THE QUESTION WINS
  • "What is going on / what do you make of this" → Read
  • "Why did it drop / how do you find the cause" → Diagnose
  • "How would you increase / improve / design for" → Design
  • "Where do you start / from scratch / first week" → 0 to 1
  • "What is wrong with / review / compare" → Critique
  • "Would you / what do you cut / respond to" → Trade-off
When it goes wrong · say this
  • Frozen: "Let me think out loud for a moment." Then name the type again.
  • Missing data: "I'll assume X and move on. I'd confirm it with Y."
  • Lost the thread: "Let me step back and map what I know."
  • Want validation: "My read is X. Tell me if you see it differently."
Never say
  • "I feel lost." (Say the line above instead.)
  • "Is that correct?" / "my best guess" / "am I missing something?"
  • Ask for a hint. State an assumption instead.
  • "It's unsolvable." End on the wrap, always.

One scenario takes 4 to 6 minutes. One beat takes 30 to 60 seconds. Solutions get the last 5 minutes, never less.

A whole whiteboard round in 9 steps and 60 minutes. Use it for Design and 0 to 1 problems.
